x: New member Denzil Winsborrow (13 foot + Pole Vaulter/6 foot High Jumper) who comes from St.Vincent is seen in action at one of our Sunday morning competitions at Battersea Park.

Denzil Winsborrow has been Vaulting and jumping extremely well. The sight of him dashing from the Pole Vault to the High Jump, both being held at the same time at the 'Vancouver' gave us something to enthuse about whilst our other men were affected by the conditions.
Our only win of the day came from Denzil Winsborrow in the Pole Vault clearing 10'8" but with the potential of clearing a far greater height than this.

The best performance of the day was from Denzil Winsborrow, an athlete who promises so much in the near future, clearing 11'6" to win the Pole Vault and beat a number of formidable opponents who had the advantage of fibre glass poles.

Denzil Winsborrow and Barry Townsend filled 2nd and 4th places in the Pole Vault and also scored heavily in the High Jump. Top points scorer of the day, though, was Nicholas Head with 3rd in the Javelin and 5th in the Shot and Discus, both the latter being close to his best ever.

Derek Wade made 2nd in the Long Jump, Denzil Winsborrow vaulted into 4th place despite a treacherous wind that removed the bar without any help from the competitors, and Barry Townsend recorded his best marks of the season with a 16.5 High Hurdles effort and a 5'11" High Jump.
Our pole vaulters Barry Townsend and Denzil Winsborrow will certainly master the fibre glass pole and then (not wanting to be corny) "the sky's the limit".

… Nick Head (Javelin), Derek Wade (Long Jump), Brian King (Javelin), Frank Glass (Discus), Bob Couillault (Triple Jump), Denzil Winsborrow (Pole Vault and High Jump) and Barry Townsend (High Jump and Pole Vault).…

Tony Brooks was the eventual winner in the fastest race with 62.0 secs. with Denzil Winsborrow, after falling, a close second. I am sure that three of the competitors for this event will break 60 seconds during the summer which will be very useful for our A & B strings in the National league.

We have never had it so good in this event with Arnold Bent (Junior) already clearing 6'1½" this season Barry Townsend 5'10", Denzil Winsborrow 5'8" and Shola Ipaye 5'8" we could well have both A and B strings over 6 feet.

John Thresher running his first track race over 1500 metres produced a time equivalent to a 4.08 mile and showed great promise for the coming season. Encouraging performances were also shown by Denzil Winsborrow and Bob Couillault who both did sub-60 seconds in the 440 hurdles.
Denzil Winsborrow did a season's best 16.8 to take second place in the 120 yds hurdles and got another silver in the pole vault with 10'-6".
Adrian Major ran the mile and 3 miles, Tony Brooks the half mile,triple jump and both relays, Denzil Winsborrow 3 events and Bob Couillault 3 events.

CENTRE RIGHT: Denzil Winsborrow snatches 2nd place in the 'A' 120yds hurdles. BOTTOM LEFT: Bill Kerr ponders his heaving chest while Tony Brooks sorts out a relay quartet with coach Dave Ansell (hidden).
Denzil Winsborrow had a busy afternoon with third in the high hurdles, an event in which he is rapidly improving, and in the high jump, and was also 4th in the pole vault.
TOP RIGHT: Tony Brooks finishs 3rd in the 440 (B). BOTTOM LEFT: Denzil Winsborrow wins high jump (A) with p.b. 6'-2". BOTTOM RIGHT: Arnold Bent win high jump (B) with 5'-10".
Denzil Winsborrow will be back in action for the Club next year (pole vault, hurdles, High jump) after a successful year of studying, gaining him entrance to Brighton University.

At the recent London Schools Meeting was DENZIL WINSBORROW, an all-rounder for Belgrave in the sixties. Denzil is now teaching in South London but spends his spare time playing cricket for Blackheath.
